parameters.description: IP address of the default gateway for the provisioning network. WHAT: the gateway handed to bare-metal hosts over DHCP so they can route to external networks during inspection and provisioning. WHEN: optional, and only honoured when platform.baremetal.provisioningNetwork is Managed (installer-managed DHCP); it is accepted but ignored when provisioningNetwork is Unmanaged or Disabled. FORMAT: a single IPv4 or IPv6 address. IMPORTANT: Red Hat documents three constraints — the gateway must be within platform.baremetal.provisioningNetworkCIDR, must be outside platform.baremetal.provisioningDHCPRange, and must not be the same address as the provisioning IP. EXAMPLE: 172.22.0.254 for a provisioningNetworkCIDR of 172.22.0.0/24 with a provisioningDHCPRange of 172.22.0.10,172.22.0.100. New in OpenShift 4.22.

conditionals.omitWhen: platform.baremetal.provisioningNetwork is Unmanaged or Disabled — openshift-install 4.22.16 accepts the field in that case but ignores it, so emitting it would be misleading
conditionals.visibility: Optional; only meaningful when the provisioning network is installer-managed
conditionals.note: Red Hat documents that the gateway must be within provisioningNetworkCIDR, outside provisioningDHCPRange, and different from the provisioning IP. These are documented product constraints; the installer's DHCP-overlap check is inert against the shipped 4.22.16 binary (delta ledger D1), so no UI validation may claim the installer rejects an overlapping value.

citations.docTitle: Provisioning [metal3.io/v1alpha1]
OpenShift Installer 4.22 Source Code

parameters.versionNotes: Introduced at 4.22. Mechanically: pkg/types/baremetal/platform.go Platform.ProvisioningNetworkGateway, string, omitempty, +optional, +kubebuilder:validation:Format=ip, with NO feature gate; absent from the exact 4.21.35 release source, and the 4.22.16 release carries "OCPBUGS-78151: Add provisioningNetworkGateway field to install-config". Documented by Red Hat at 4.22 in Provisioning APIs Chapter 13 "Provisioning [metal3.io/v1alpha1]" §13.1.1 .spec: "ProvisioningNetworkGateway is the IP address of the default gateway for the provisioning network. This gateway is provided to baremetal hosts via DHCP to enable routing to external networks during inspection and provisioning. This field is optional and only used when ProvisioningNetwork is set to Managed. The gateway IP must be within the ProvisioningNetworkCIDR but outside of the ProvisioningDHCPRange and must not be the same as ProvisioningIP." The same chapter at 4.20 and 4.21 does not contain the field, which is why minVersion is 4.22. Exact-binary behaviour against openshift-install 4.22.16: accepted with provisioningNetwork: Managed; "not-an-ip" REJECTED as not a valid IP; accepted and ignored with provisioningNetwork: Disabled. DO NOT present the DHCP-range overlap rule as installer-enforced: the installer's own check (pkg/types/baremetal/validation/platform.go) is INERT against the shipped 4.22.16 binary — a gateway inside the allocated DHCP range was accepted, and the pre-existing clusterProvisioningIP check of the same code shape is equally inert, so this is a shared mechanism rather than a 4.22 regression (mechanical delta ledger D1). The within-CIDR, network-address and broadcast-address checks were not individually binary-probed and must likewise not be claimed as installer-enforced. The three constraints above are recorded as DOCUMENTED Red Hat product semantics, which is what they are.

parameters.description: Determines whether DNS records for api, api-int, and ingress are provided by the internal DNS service or externally. When set to 'Internal' (or omitted), records are provided by the internal infrastructure. When set to 'External', records must be configured by the user on a DNS server outside the cluster; External requires the OnPremDNSRecords feature gate to be enabled and loadBalancer.type=UserManaged. External mode is not currently configured by this application.
parameters.notes: Cataloged for documentation completeness. The OnPremDNSRecords feature gate can be enabled via TechPreviewNoUpgrade, DevPreviewNoUpgrade, or CustomNoUpgrade with an explicit featureGates entry. External mode also requires loadBalancer.type=UserManaged. This application omits the field entirely (defaulting to Internal) because it does not configure the required feature gate or loadBalancer.type selection.
